text.p: Scientific-Atlanta Inc said on Tuesday that a federal judge awarded the company a combined $25.4 million judgment against a major seller of altered cable set-top terminals, but the company expects to receive a nominal amount of the award.

The company said that Jeffrey Fenley, an individual doing business as National Electronic Wholesalers, was ordered to pay Scientific-Atlanta $21.3 million for violating laws that bar the sale of altered cable boxes and $4.1 million for trademark infringement.
Scientific-Atlanta said National Electronic Wholesalers also was issued a permanent injunction barring it from advertising or selling any device for gaining unauthorized access to cable service.
Scientific-Atlanta said the judgment was the first award against a company that sells altered cable boxes for violating trademark rights of an original set-top terminal maker.
The altered cable boxes are rigged so that their users can receive free cable television.
